title: Render modes
summary: Where a component runs (server or browser) and whether it is interactive.

predict.title: No render mode
predict.answer: **Count: 0.** Nothing happens. Without `@rendermode`, the page is **static SSR**: the server sends HTML and disposes the component. The `@onclick` handler is never wired up, because no C# is listening in the browser or on the server. There is no error, which is why this bug is easy to miss.

predict.title: Interactive Server
predict.answer: **Count: 3.** Each click is sent to the server over the SignalR **WebSocket**. The server runs `count++`, re-renders, and sends back only the **diff** (the changed text). You don't need `StateHasChanged()`: Blazor re-renders automatically after an event handler.

predict.title: How many times?
predict.answer: **Twice, both in the server console** (the terminal where `dotnet run` runs). The first time is during **prerendering** (static HTML). The second is when the circuit starts and the component becomes interactive. With `prerender: false`, it prints only once.

predict.title: WebAssembly console
predict.body:
Same as C, but the component is in the `.Client` project and uses:

```razor
@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly
```

**After one full page load, where does "C initialized" appear?**
predict.answer: **Once in the server console** (prerendering happens on the server) and **once in the browser's dev tools console** (the WebAssembly render runs in the browser, so `Console.WriteLine` goes there).

practice.text:
**Create the app** in your own folder (for example `learn-blazor/level-01-render-modes/code`):

```bash
dotnet new blazor -n RenderModesLab -int Auto
```

You get two projects: `RenderModesLab` (server) and `RenderModesLab.Client` (the code sent to the browser).
practice.hint: If the options are different in your SDK, run `dotnet new blazor --help`. `-int Auto` enables both Server and WebAssembly, so you can try all four modes.

practice.text: **Create `/static`** in the server project: a counter button and a line showing `RendererInfo.Name` and `RendererInfo.IsInteractive`. Use **no** `@rendermode`.
**Create `/server`**: the same page with `@rendermode InteractiveServer`, in the server project.
**Create `/wasm`** with `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly`, and **`/auto`** with `@rendermode InteractiveAuto`. Both go in the **`.Client`** project.
practice.hint: If the page returns 404, check that the file is in the `.Client` project and that `Program.cs` calls `.AddAdditionalAssemblies(...)` with the client assembly (the template already does this).

practice.text: **Run the app** (`dotnet run` in the server project). Visit all four pages and write down whether the count changes, and what `Name` and `IsInteractive` show. Put this in the Note tab's free notes.
**Dev tools:** on `/server`, find the WebSocket in the Network tab (filter: WS). On `/wasm`, find the `.wasm` downloads. On `/static`, use View Source and check that the full HTML is there.
On `/server`, add `Console.WriteLine` in `OnInitialized`. Reload once and **count the lines** in the terminal.
Disable prerendering with `@rendermode @(new InteractiveServerRenderMode(prerender: false))`. Reload and **count again**. Also look at View Source: what changed?
practice.hint: Without prerendering, the server sends almost no HTML for the component, and it appears only when the circuit is ready.

challenge.statement:
In a **new** Blazor Web App, build from scratch a `/modes` page using **Interactive Server** that shows:

- the render mode name and whether it is interactive
- a click counter
- the time of the last click

Run it with `dotnet run` and check that it works before you finish. Then answer the three questions below.

questions.text: Why does the button work on /server but not on /static?
questions.modelAnswer: A static page is **only HTML**: the server renders it and disposes the component, so **no circuit** and no C# are listening for the click. On `/server`, a SignalR circuit keeps the component alive on the server and receives events.

questions.text: On /wasm, where does the C# code run, and what does the browser download first?
questions.modelAnswer: **In the browser**, on .NET compiled to WebAssembly. First the browser downloads the **.NET runtime and the app's assemblies** (the `_framework/*.wasm` and `.dll` files).

questions.text: Why did the console line print twice before you disabled prerendering?
questions.modelAnswer: Because of **prerendering**: the component is rendered once on the server as static HTML, and then **again** when it becomes interactive, so `OnInitialized` runs both times.

rubric.passLooksLike: `@onclick` increments the count, with no needless `StateHasChanged()`
A field stores the time and the page displays it
Q1: static = HTML only, no circuit. Q2: runs in the browser after runtime + assemblies download. Q3: prerender on the server, then again when interactive

interview.question: What are the Blazor render modes?
interview.modelAnswer: Static SSR (the default: HTML only, not interactive), Interactive Server (runs on the server over a SignalR circuit), Interactive WebAssembly (runs in the browser), and Interactive Auto (Server first, then WebAssembly once it is downloaded).

interview.question: When would you choose Server over WebAssembly?
interview.modelAnswer: When you want a fast first load, direct access to server resources (database, secrets), or small client devices, and users have a stable, low-latency connection. Typical for internal business apps.

interview.question: When would you choose WebAssembly over Server?
interview.modelAnswer: When you want no round trip per UI event, offline support, less server memory and connection load, or hosting as static files (a CDN). The trade-off is a larger first download, and that all client code is public.

interview.question: What does Auto mode do?
interview.modelAnswer: It starts with Interactive Server for a fast first render while downloading the WebAssembly bundle in the background. Later visits use WebAssembly. The component must live in the `.Client` project and work in both places.

interview.question: What is prerendering and what problem can it cause?
interview.modelAnswer: The server renders interactive components to HTML first, for a fast first paint and SEO, then renders them again when they become interactive. Lifecycle methods run twice, so data can load twice or flicker. Fix it with `prerender: false` or by persisting state with `[PersistentState]` (.NET 10).

interview.question: How does the UI update in Interactive Server?
interview.modelAnswer: The browser sends the event over a SignalR WebSocket. The server runs the handler, re-renders the component, compares it with the previous render tree, and sends only the diff. The browser then patches the DOM.

interview.question: Why does a button do nothing on a static page?
interview.modelAnswer: With static SSR, the component is rendered once to HTML and disposed. No circuit or WebAssembly runtime is listening, so `@onclick` is never wired up. It fails silently.

interview.question: How do you tell which mode a component is running in?
interview.modelAnswer: Look for `@rendermode` on the component, on its usage, or globally on `<Routes>` in `App.razor`. At runtime, check `RendererInfo.Name` / `RendererInfo.IsInteractive` (and `AssignedRenderMode`).
